doc.title: Vince Lateano interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 8, 2002

title: Al Cohn and the Half Note stories
summary: Al Cohn's banker looks and wry reply, and stories of Cohn and Zoot Sims at the Half Note.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Yeah right. And people listen with their eyes. And hopefully musicians listen with their ears. You know I’ll never forget Al Cohn is probably on that list I played with Al Cohn, he was a favorite, man I loved that guy. And I remember one night we were playing somewhere. Did you know Al or did you ever see him?
I saw him in Rochester years ago.
All right. Al was a very straight looking guy.
Yeah. He looked like a banker or something.

Somebody said to him, I swear to God, somebody said to him on a break you know, you always get — “Gee you don’t look like a jazz musician, you look like a banker.” And you know Al was very droll. And he accepted it and he smiled. And he came over to me and he says, “So what does a jazz musician look like?” You know Al. And it’s true. They just want you to be — I shouldn’t say that — but I guess some of them want, some of the people that come out, they like the B movie down and out I guess.
Um hum. A little anguish. They like to see a little anguish.
Yeah. Some pain you know. Al was great. Oh I loved him. He was —
Now he had — I think I saw him with was it Zoot Sims?
And he had the thing with —

Oh he told stories about him and Zoot at the Half Note in New York. I was only at that club once and I heard – who did I hear there in the early 60s, like Lennie Tristano or somebody you know. I just happened to be in town. And it was a funny kind of a club that I think you walked in and you walked around the bar but the bandstand was above the bar. So the guys, the bartenders would be beneath you. So they had this thing worked out where he and Zoot and the bartender, this character, would give them drinks and when they were done they had this routine where they would play and they would drop it, drop the glass, and he’d walk by and he would catch it. © Fillius Jazz Archive -13-
I mean they had this whole thing. I’m sorry I missed — somebody might have filmed it, this whole choreography of the drinks going back and forth.
